run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-18T01:02:44Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: Frontend's RequestErrorRate alert is explained by a downstream cart/valkey failure, not by a frontend-internal fault. Frontend span error rate (status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR) was 0 at every 2-minute sample from 00:39:44Z through 01:01:44Z and then rose to 0.089/s at 01:03:44Z, 1.42/s at 01:07:44Z, 1.88/s at 01:09:44Z and 1.03/s at 01:13:44Z, concentrated on its cart operations (POST /api/cart, GET /api/cart, executing api route (pages) /api/cart, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem and GetCart). The cart service itself began emitting error spans on POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem and GetCart from the 01:05-01:07Z samples, and its pod log repeatedly shows 'Wasn't able to connect to redis'. The redis-compatible dependency pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft is not Ready: container valkey-cart was last terminated OOMKilled (exit code 137) at 01:05:43Z with restartCount 4 and is now CrashLoopBackOff, and the valkey-cart Service endpoint has no ready address (only notReadyAddress 100.96.5.138). The fault was applied by Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress in namespace chaos-mesh, which spawned a new StressChaos roughly every minute from 01:01:38Z, each reporting 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft/valkey-cart'. The pod cgroup max memory usage (10,493,952 bytes) sits just above the valkey-cart Deployment's 10Mi limit (10,485,760 bytes) while the valkey container's own peak was ~5.58MB, consistent with an injected memory stressor pushing the pod cgroup over its limit. All nodes report MemoryPressure False and the flagd fault flags (cartFailure and others) are at defaultVariant off, so node pressure and flagd injection are rejected as causes. Checkout and frontend-proxy also show their own error spans from 01:07:00Z; the frontend-proxy tie to the frontend 5xx is a timing-based hypothesis only.

claims.text: Frontend span error rate (status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR, all frontend operations) was 0 at every 2-minute sample from 00:39:44Z through 01:01:44Z, then rose to 0.089/s at 01:03:44Z, 1.42/s at 01:07:44Z, 1.88/s at 01:09:44Z and 1.03/s at 01:13:44Z; total frontend span rate was ~44/s before the rise, so the error share grew inside a roughly stable request mix.

Frontend's own error spans in 00:55:00Z-01:14:00Z are concentrated on cart calls: increase of 153.5 on span 'POST /api/cart', 211.2 on 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart', 124.7 on 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem', 86.5 on 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart', 57.7 on 'GET /api/cart', plus 33.0 on 'POST /api/checkout' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder'.

The cart service emitted its own error spans on 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem' and 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart': 0 at the 01:03:00Z sample, 0.016/s at 01:05:00Z, 0.184/0.181/s at 01:07:00Z and ~0.214/0.160/s at 01:13:00Z; EmptyCart error rate stayed ~0.004/s.

The cart application container log of pod cart-755465879b-4p8d9 repeatedly shows 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' followed by "Error status code '{StatusCode}' with detail '{Detail}' raised." between 01:09:32Z and 01:10:07Z, interleaved with normal GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync calls.

Pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft is not Ready (Ready=False, reason ContainersNotReady since 01:05:43Z); container valkey-cart lastState.terminated has reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, startedAt 01:05:32Z, finishedAt 01:05:43Z, restartCount 4, and its current state is waiting with reason CrashLoopBackOff ('back-off 1m20s restarting failed container=valkey-cart').

Warning BackOff events for pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft ('Back-off restarting failed container valkey-cart') occur 22 times from 01:02:42Z to 01:10:00Z, with 'Created container: valkey-cart' and 'Started container valkey-cart' events at 01:07:16Z-01:07:18Z.

Chaos Mesh Schedule 'otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress' (namespace chaos-mesh) reported reason Spawned repeatedly with messages 'Create new object: otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress-flgz4' at 01:01:38Z, ckxt6 01:02:38Z, w8p5x 01:03:38Z, nt6th 01:04:38Z, 95xf6 01:05:38Z, ltcpd 01:06:38Z, v75mv 01:08:28Z and psc57 01:09:23Z, plus Forbid events while the previous object was still running.

The StressChaos objects spawned by that Schedule target valkey-cart: each shows reason Applied with message 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft/valkey-cart' (flgz4 01:01:38Z, ckxt6 01:02:38Z, w8p5x 01:03:38Z, nt6th 01:04:38Z, 95xf6 01:05:38Z) and 'Successfully recover chaos ...' about 55s later (01:02:33Z, 01:03:33Z, 01:04:33Z, 01:05:33Z, 01:06:33Z); the ltcpd (01:06:38Z) and psc57 (01:09:23Z) runs instead reported 'Failed to apply chaos: ... no running task found: task 26cfff7d...' and 'task bf44a508...'.

For pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft the pod-level cgroup container_memory_max_usage_bytes reached 10,493,952 bytes in 00:55:00Z-01:14:00Z while the per-container valkey-cart maxima were only 3.15MB-5.58MB; the valkey-cart Deployment declares limits cpu 10m / memory 10Mi and requests cpu 2m / memory 4Mi, and shows no available replicas while cart and frontend each show 1 available.

The valkey-cart Service endpoints have no ready addresses: valkey-cart has ready_addresses [] and not_ready ['100.96.5.138'], while cart (100.96.5.38), frontend (100.96.1.50) and frontend-proxy (100.96.1.169) each have a ready address.

All five nodes (i-011a5a806da9fd225, i-0a7fb5c090766247e, i-0d211959f7bf532cd, i-0f0dbfb8b5d3de987, i-0f646caed8aca795a) report MemoryPressure False and DiskPressure False; the valkey-cart pod runs on i-0d211959f7bf532cd.

Other services carry their own error spans in the same window: checkout error rate was 0 before 01:05:00Z and 0.073/s at 01:07:00Z, 0.132/s at 01:09:00Z and ~0.097/s at 01:11-01:13, on operations 'oteldemo.CartService/GetCart', 'oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart', 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' and 'HTTP POST'; frontend-proxy error rate rose from a ≤0.02/s baseline (00:40-01:01) to 0.84/s at 01:07:00Z and 0.96/s at 01:13:00Z.

Frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-x9gbm is Running and ready with restartCount 0, as are cart-755465879b-4p8d9 and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-4ctlp; the only pod in otel-demo with a non-zero restart count or unready state is valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft (ready false, restarts 4).

Not every error signal is new: ad shows ~0.0037/s and fraud-detection ~0.0037/s span errors both well before the rise (00:45:00Z, 00:51:00Z, 01:01:00Z) and after it, indicating pre-existing background errors on flagd EventStream/Resolve spans unrelated to the cart failure.

flagd fault injection is not the trigger: the live flagd-config ConfigMap (demo.flagd.json) has defaultVariant 'off' for cartFailure ('Fail cart service'), paymentFailure, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems and every other flag.
Node-level memory pressure is not the cause of the valkey OOMKill: every node reports MemoryPressure False and DiskPressure False.

The frontend warning is a downstream consequence of cart's redis dependency being killed: the Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress injects a memory stressor into the valkey-cart pod cgroup (which maxed at 10,493,952 bytes against the 10Mi limit), the valkey-cart container is OOMKilled (exit 137) and stays CrashLoopBackOff with no ready endpoint from 01:02:42Z, cart logs 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' and returns errors on AddItem/GetCart, and frontend's cart API routes and gRPC CartService calls then carry error spans — matching the first Schedule Spawned event at 01:01:38Z against the last zero-error frontend sample at 01:01:44Z.

frontend-proxy's error spans are probably the failing responses frontend generated for its cart API routes; this link is inferred only from concurrent timing (proxy errors rose together with frontend ones from 01:07:00Z) and the HTTP status behind those spans was not observed.

Human follow-up: stop or delete the Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress in namespace chaos-mesh and let valkey-cart recover, then re-check the frontend RequestErrorRate, cart error spans and valkey-cart endpoint readiness.

Human follow-up: reconsider the valkey-cart Deployment's memory limit of 10Mi with a 4Mi request — it leaves essentially no headroom, so a transient memory spike terminates the redis-compatible cart store and takes cart, checkout and frontend down with it.

gaps: The alerting rule RequestErrorRate could not be read: list_prometheus_rules filtered by rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no rules (no_data), so the expression and the metric behind the annotation value 'current: 3.0222222222222217' are unverified.

Jaeger could not supply error traces: traces_search_by_tags for service frontend with error=true over 00:02:44Z-01:21:32Z returned no traces (no_data), and a plain traces_search returned 317 spans whose data covers only 00:41:42.488Z-00:41:45.651Z, so span-level error tags/messages for 01:02-01:14 are unknown and error evidence comes from trace-derived metrics only.

The Chaos Mesh Schedule and StressChaos objects are custom resources outside the readable kinds, so the stressor's size, workers, duration and selector are unknown; only their events were observed and those events cover 00:44:44Z-01:10:00Z.

Trace-derived metrics end at 01:13:44Z although the query ran to 01:21:32Z; the frontend error rate and the final total span rate (11.0/s at 01:13:44Z vs ~30/s) after that point are unknown, as is whether the errors were still ongoing.

valkey-cart container logs returned no lines (status no_data: current instance read 0 bytes, previous instance unavailable), and the frontend container log query returned no lines (no_data), so the OOM trigger could not be confirmed from container log output.
The change_history integration is not available, so who created or modified Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress and when is unknown.
Kubernetes objects were read at query time (~01:21-01:22Z), not during the incident; cluster state between 01:02 and 01:14 is inferred from events, metrics and current object status.
